name: Alien Worlds Framework
verdict_reason: It is a world-generation framework (brief section 4 test 5: dissonant; section 2: no worldgen), yet it is wired into how the campaign's SOURCE world was made. Our src/RimUtinni/UtinniPatches/Patches/JawaWorld_BiomeMix.xml patches the TidallyLocked PlanetTypeDef of `7f.alienworlds.tidallylocked` (its header: kept because it configures the game that produces the source world Ash'karr is painted from), UtinniPatches About.xml forceLoadAfter names both mods (lines 81-82), and tidally_locked_world.md records the mod as worldgen-only (FieldPatcher hooks WorldGenStep_Terrain; nothing recomputes temperature at runtime, so it cannot reach the hand-painted frozen save). Runtime need is therefore nil but the authoring/remake path may still use it, and removing it unguarded breaks UtinniPatches' patch target. Held until the final paint/remake settles whether the source world is ever regenerated (brief section 5.8).

verdict_reason: UI convenience over 550 mods' worth of descriptions; no gameplay effect, so it passes the 7-question test trivially (brief §4 test 4). Description parsing happens at load or on display, but no tick FLAG exists; its load cost is UNMEASURED. Nothing of ours references it.
open_questions: Our own mods' descriptions will be auto-linked; the player may see links to donor defs we mean to retire. Cosmetic only.

name: Faction Customizer
verdict_reason: Two roles. As an authoring aid for the one hand-made world (relocate and rename settlements, set goodwill) it is useful until the final paint, mirroring the Worldbuilder example in RUBRIC §8. As a player-facing editor it is dissonant: players receive a fixed world and fixed factions (brief §1, §2 no worldgen). Design uses it in one place: design/Jawa/worldbuilding/faction_roster_v2.md (lines 131-140) names it as the only candidate mechanism for graded goodwill, marked v2 and gated, reading baseGoodwill/naturalGoodwillOffset from its assembly. restraining_bolt_technical.md (line 269) also lists it as touching the goodwill situation workers.
needs_owner: This mod lets a player rename factions, move settlements and rewrite the world. Is it only a tool for you while building the world (remove it before release), or do you want players to have it?
open_questions: Load order is cited as 145 in faction_roster_v2.md and 147 in restraining_bolt_technical.md; FULL.LATEST position is 134 (full_latest_position). The docs are stale; not resolved here.
holds_it_in: world authoring until the paint pass
owner_ruling_note: Authoring/scouting tool: kept for our own use until shipping, removed from the player list at release.

name: Camera+
verdict_reason: The map is the owner's main viewport on a 550-mod list and Camera+ is by the Harmony author (MIT, pushed 2026-08-28). Our own tooling treats it as a first-class case: src/RimMandrake/Utils/modset_builder.py (lines 77-80) says debug sets carry ray1203.simplecamerasetting for zoom, which is incompatible with Camera+, so a tier that wants Camera+ must say so. That is a measured interaction, not a conflict in the full list (ray1203 is not in the universe).
open_questions: Debug tiers use a different zoom mod; any tier containing both would conflict.
holds_it_in: modset_builder.py zoom policy (explicit exemption needed for Camera+)

name: Enable Oversized Weapons
verdict_reason: Cosmetic enabler for large weapons; the scenario keeps lightsaber and blaster weapons (brief §2) and the stat-normalization audit (line 170) filed it as "weapon draw size, no gameplay number". Our weapon art may rely on drawSize rendering; if so it quietly depends on this mod, but src/ shows no reference. Repo link is a name-search match (INFERRED), pushed 2026-01-13.
open_questions: Do any RimStarWars weapon defs set drawSize above the vanilla range? If yes, tag this as a dependency.
holds_it_in: possible implicit dependence: our weapon defs that set drawSize (UNVERIFIED)

name: Configurable Techprints
verdict_reason: Our research pipeline writes through it: src/RimMandrake/Utils/research_manifest_validate.py (lines 661-670) attributes techprintCount to this mod, and TECHPRINT_FACTION_GATING_1 (items) says it is ruled and routes through this mod's settings (OPUS5_HANDOFF.md lines 275-277). It implements the four research access classes the owner ruled (common, jawa-special, ship-only, faction-held), so removing it deletes the gating mechanism. GPL-3.0, repo AnthonyChenevier/ConfigurableTechprints, pushed 2025-07-20.
open_questions: GPL-3.0: do not copy code into RM_ mods; if we ever want our own, write it fresh.

name: Deteriorable Filter
verdict_reason: Tiny XML-style filter (one DLL, no Harmony flags) that helps sort a salvage yard and keep valuable deteriorating items indoors. Desert/Salvage crew with finite indoor space: mild resonance. No source link found (steam-only), but there is little to break.

name: Custom Room Names
verdict_reason: Prior audit graded it "trivial QoL: name your rooms" (outgrown_audit_2026-08-30.md line 100) and nothing contradicts that. On a ship where the crew lives aboard, naming rooms of a gravship is a natural use. The two comp-tick FLAGs belong to a few placed panels, so tick load scales with panels placed, not the map. Placed panels live in saves (save placement UNMEASURED), which matters only for a retirement.
holds_it_in: nothing depends on it; placed Room Panels persist in saves

name: Cozy Fires
verdict_reason: Comfort bonus from fires suits a desert nights-are-cold survival crew. The 179-op patch body is wide but only touches vanilla/Royalty/VFE defs; none of ours (patches_ours_refs 0, patched_by empty). Steam-only, no source. No ruling mentions it, and heat is unaffected (one kind of heat, vanilla only; this is comfort, not temperature).

name: Cybranian - Ideology Virtues
verdict_reason: Our ideoligion is authored and fixed (src/Jawa/ideoligion/MandrakeJawa.xtp lists the mod in its export mod list at line 113 and 1281, but only in the mod list, not in a precept: grep of the .xtp finds exactly 2 mentions), and skills/rimworld-ideoligion/references/authoring.md line 337 classes it among "long tail, 1-3 precepts each". It adds Issue/Precept defs that appear in the ideology designer; with a fixed ideoligion the designer is not used by players, so its content is dead weight unless the authored ideoligion includes its precepts (it does not, INFERRED from the 2 mod-list mentions). The patches into Ideology (18 ops) are the risk. Exit: confirm it is unused by every authored ideoligion, then drop.

The repo was nevertheless pushed 2026-10-07 and the mod logs 0 errors in the measured session, so it works today. name: Biome Compatibility Project
verdict_reason: It directly contradicts the roster law: biome casts are hand-built per biome sitting and an animal belongs to ONE biome (CLAUDE.md "An animal belongs to ONE biome"; brief §2 evictions stopped, roster changes at each sitting). Its code mutates the same fields: the closed item WILD_ANIMALS_PADDED_LISTS_1 measured every wildAnimals list padded to 1024 records and named this mod "suspect", and src/RimMandrake/Utils/biome_wildbiomes_evictions.py exists to undo the effect. Our own tooling already refuses it: modset_builder.py TIERS["pyrelands"] puts it in `forbid`, and Pyrelands/Source/WildPlantAllowlist.cs is a runtime guard built because it (with other biome mods) injects foreign flora. Retirement is cheap: def_total 0, no dependants, no placed Things.

verdict_reason: Slave trade fits the Hutt-ledger setting (brief §1) and the mod is tiny and XML-driven, with a verified MIT repo (emipa606/SYRMoreSlaves, pushed 2025-08-22). The tension is arithmetic: the pillars fix the crew at about 3-8 and tie scale to the ship, and more purchasable slaves is a labour-supply lever (brief §2 anti-exponential). No ruling covers it, so KEEP is the conservative verdict until the owner answers the question below.

verdict_reason: It is the curation instrument the scenario is built on: brief §1 pillars say curation is "by Cherry Picker trimming, not uninstalling", and §3 lists "keep the mod, cut the content" as a legitimate verdict shape. Our tooling hard-codes it: src/RimMandrake/Utils/preload_check.py has HARD_RULES (Cherry Picker must precede oskarpotocki.vanillafactionsexpanded.core) and CHERRYPICKER_MAX_INDEX = 40, and design/Jawa/fauna/gen_cast_patch.py references it. The brief names Vanilla Genetics Expanded and VFE-Insectoids 2 as "cherry-pick the engine, keep the creatures" cases, which need it.
